title: Smart Contract Security Fundamentals
learning_outcomes: Explain the main ideas in Smart Contract Security Fundamentals and correctly use the key terms in context.
Build or inspect a minimal Solidity example that demonstrates the lesson concepts.
Test representative failure cases and describe version, security, or operational assumptions where relevant.

overview_visual.alt_text: A two-column ordered roadmap for Module 14: Smart Contract Security Fundamentals; it lists all 21 source-syllabus lesson topics by number.
overview_visual.caption: Module 14 roadmap: Security Principles for Smart Contracts; Threat Modeling and Trust Boundaries; Identifying Attack Surfaces; Access-Control Vulnerabilities; Reentrancy and Cross-Function Reentrancy; Checks-Effects-Interactions; Unchecked External Call Results; Arithmetic Errors and Unexpected Numeric Behavior; Denial of Service and Gas-Limit Risks; Transaction Ordering and MEV Concepts; Front-Running and Transaction-Order Dependence; Oracle Manipulation and Stale Data; Insecure Randomness; Signature Replay and Domain Separation; Signature Malleability and Validation; Incorrect Authorization and tx.origin Misuse; Uninitialized State and Constructor Mistakes; Delegatecall and Storage-Collision Risks; Unsafe Upgrades and Privileged-Role Risks; Public Data, Privacy, and False Confidentiality Assumptions; Security Reviews, Vulnerability Classification, and Mitigations. Work through the topics in order, then implement a small example and verify assumptions.

notes: Preserves numbered syllabus topics 175–195 from the attached Solidity PDF. Track: core. All content is draft pending subject-matter review.
